channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Drax, Brookfield and Radiant target a 1GW AI data centre at Drax Power Station — £20bn-plus if built in full
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Drax Group, Brookfield and Radiant signed an agreement on November 3, 2026 to develop an AI data centre of more than 1GW at Drax Power Station in North Yorkshire, with Brookfield estimating total potential investment above £20 billion including chips — but the first 100MW phase still needs planning approval, a tenant and final investment decisions.

item.title: NVIDIA brings physical and agentic AI to cities: 150+ resident-service deployments in Spain, 17,000 cameras in Malaysia
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA said on November 3, 2026 that it and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide, from resident-service agents in Spain to vision agents scaling toward 17,000 cameras in Malaysia — with shared infrastructure and digital twins tying the projects together.

item.title: AGIBOT unveils GO-3 Preview: a robot model that tops three benchmarks — and keeps learning on the job
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AGIBOT unveiled GO-3 Preview on November 3, 2026, an embodied foundation model it says ranks first on RoboDojo, RoboTwin and RoboColiseum. The model will be fully open-sourced by the end of 2026.

item.title: Granter raises €1.6M to take its AI grant-writing assistant across Europe
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Granter has raised €1.6 million, led by 3XP Global, to expand its AI-powered platform that helps businesses identify, apply for, and manage European public funding — work the company says can fall from weeks to under an hour.

item.title: 2CRSi lands a €60M+ order for 83 NVIDIA B300 servers from Exaion — sovereign inference, delivered by December
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: 2CRSi announced on November 3, 2026, a binding order worth more than €60 million from Exaion for 83 NVIDIA HGX B300 AI servers, plus storage and maintenance, with all 83 to be delivered by the end of December 2026 as Exaion expands from model training into private on-premises inference.

item.title: One tiny binary, any model, plain English: hands-on with Shim
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Shim (Balanov/shim, MIT, 383 GitHub stars) is a 7.29 MiB static Go binary that wires any OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic model API, MCP servers and Agent Skills into one terminal harness with no daemon, no TUI and no telemetry. This guide installs v0.1.0, runs shim setup, adds a local model and a hosted model, tests both, runs a read-only agent task, connects an MCP server, installs a skill, sets up the local-model command router and permissions, and resumes a session, with the safety limits the project states itself.

item.title: PATEO puts Doubao and Nemotron in the car: an AI Box on NVIDIA Thor that runs without the cloud
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: PATEO announced on November 3, 2026, an AI Box built on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor that runs ByteDance's 35-billion-parameter Doubao model and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 speech recognition locally in the vehicle, with a project nomination pointing to mass production in the second quarter of 2027.

item.title: Cohere launches Defence AI Accelerator in Singapore to move sovereign AI from pilots to operations
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cohere announced on November 3, 2026, a Defence AI Accelerator in Singapore to help defence organizations and other sovereign customers move AI applications from proof-of-concept to operational deployment in highly secure environments, using its models and its North agentic AI platform.

item.title: xAI's Data Bot is Grok Bot's shared data scientist — and it handled 70 hours of work in a week
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: xAI introduced Data Bot on November 2, 2026, a Team Bot in Grok Bot that queries SpaceXSI's data warehouse using skills and shared memory maintained by its data science team. The company estimates it handled about 70 hours of work in the week before publication.

item.title: Marvell to buy Lumentum for $115 billion, betting AI data centers move from copper to light
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Marvell announced a definitive agreement on November 2, 2026, to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion. Lumentum stockholders would receive 4.500 Marvell shares per share — about $1,132, a 23.9% premium to October 28 — and own about 33% of the combined company, which the companies expect to close in the first half of 2028.

item.title: ECARX and Arm sign MoU to explore high-performance AI computing for vehicles and physical AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: ECARX and Arm signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding on November 2, 2026, to jointly explore next-generation high-performance AI computing platforms for mobility and cross-industry physical-AI applications, building on SiEngine chip work that has produced millions of 7nm SE1000 units since March 2023. No chip, financial terms or timetable were announced.

item.title: OpenAI signs Magnite and PubMatic deals to fill unused ChatGPT ad space
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI has signed deals with ad-tech platforms Magnite and PubMatic to sell unsold ChatGPT advertising space, The Information reported on November 2, 2026. Advertisers will be able to set budgets, bid and upload ads through tools they already use, while OpenAI keeps control of where ads appear; financial terms were not disclosed.

item.title: Let your coding agent click real apps — without screenshots: hands-on with agent-desktop
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: agent-desktop (vercel-labs/agent-desktop, Apache-2.0, 9,703 GitHub stars) is a Rust CLI and C library that lets a coding agent read and operate macOS, Windows and Linux apps through the operating system's accessibility tree. This guide installs v1.0.2 with npm, checks permissions with agent-desktop status, snapshots Finder by ref, drills into a dense app with --skeleton and --root, clicks and types, verifies by re-snapshotting, and teaches an agent the loop with the bundled skills, with the retry and privacy rules the docs insist on.

item.title: Hydrogen-1.0: a 753B open-weight model trained on lab records reports a science win over GPT-6-Astra
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Deep Principle introduced Hydrogen-1.0 on November 2, 2026: a 753-billion-parameter open-weight model post-trained from Z.ai's GLM-5.3 on chemistry, materials and life-science data plus the company's own laboratory records. The company reports 38.3% on FrontierScience-Research against 33.3% for GPT-6-Astra — company-reported figures that have not been independently verified.

item.title: Larridin raises $30M Series A to measure whether enterprise AI spending actually pays off
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Larridin announced a $30 million Series A on November 2, 2026, led by Pelion Ventures, bringing its total funding to $47 million. The South San Francisco company connects AI cost to the work it produces, reporting more than 2 billion AI sessions measured and a median $2.4 million in AI spend optimized in the first year — company-reported figures.

item.title: CMiC unveils NexusAI: plain-language AI agents arrive in construction ERP
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: CMiC introduced NexusAI on November 2, 2026, an AI launchpad inside its NEXUS construction ERP that lets teams launch AI agents and surface ERP content by asking in plain language. Powered by the CMiC MCP Server, it runs inside existing security settings and permissions, with jobs, budgets and invoices created through a request, review and confirmation step.

item.title: ACCESS Newswire launches SPOT: seven AI agents vet every press release — and predict whether ChatGPT will cite it
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: ACCESS Newswire launched SPOT on November 2, 2026: seven AI agents that check a press release after it is written and before it is submitted. Three agents are included with every release and four are add-ons, including an LLM Visibility Score that predicts how likely ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Grok are to cite it.

item.title: Stop paying Opus to type: stretch your Claude plan with Cheap Agent
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Cheap Agent (muaaz9329/cheap-ag, MIT, 218 GitHub stars) is a Claude Code MCP server that lets Opus plan while a cheap model writes the code in a git worktree and proves it with tests. This guide installs v1.2.7 with npx cheap-agent, logs in through OpenRouter, DeepSeek, OpenCode Go or Command Code, allows one project with /cheapag:allow, runs a first delegated change, and checks the cost with /cheapag:status, plus the author's SWE-bench numbers and their limits.

item.title: 42AI exits stealth with $62.5M for a 'behavioral world model' that predicts what traders will do
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: 42AI came out of stealth on November 2, 2026 with $62.5 million in seed funding for a 'behavioral world model' that estimates the probability of what individuals will do, starting with traders at 10 large brokerages. Its headline 98% accuracy figure measures whether trading flows fall inside a predicted range, not whether each trade was called correctly.

item.title: Clark launches Clerks, autonomous AI employees for CPA audit teams, with an $11M seed round
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Clark launched Clerks on November 2, 2026: AI employees assigned to audit engagements that review documents, run tests and prepare workpapers, backed by an $11 million seed round led by Touring Capital that brings total funding to $16 million. Licensed CPAs still make the judgments and sign the opinion.

item.title: ETSI, Japan and South Korea sign letter of intent to explore a 3GPP-style AI standards partnership
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: ETSI, Japan’s TTC and South Korea’s TTA signed a letter of intent on November 2, 2026 to explore a possible industry-led AI Partnership Project modelled on 3GPP — an exploration, not yet a partnership or a published standard.

item.title: Gallium Defense emerges from stealth: €7.1M seed for an AI-native radar that spots drones 10km away
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Paris-based Gallium Defense emerged from stealth on November 2, 2026 with a €7.1 million seed round to industrialise the GDS-10, an X-band AESA radar with a software-defined, AI-native architecture designed to detect Class 1 and FPV drones at up to 10km. Orders are planned to open in the first quarter of 2027.

item.title: Abu Dhabi turns its rulebook into code: OpenAI machine-readable government pilot is already live on food imports
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Abu Dhabi and OpenAI launched a Machine-Readable Government initiative on November 2, 2026: selected policies and regulations become machine-readable so AI can assist officials with routine compliance checks. The first pilot is already in production on food imports, with officials keeping final decisions — and no financial terms disclosed.

item.title: Go.AI's Go1 MAX packs eight Blackwell GPUs into one box to serve 8,000 on-prem AI users
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Go.AI has launched the Go1 MAX, an on-premises AI appliance with eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and 768GB of GPU memory that serves up to 8,000 concurrent users from a single box, with fixed pricing, unlimited usage and a 15-minute setup. It is available to order now.

item.title: Your own always-on AI bot, on any model: hands-on with AnyModelBot
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: AnyModelBot (modelflare-ai/AnyModelBot, MIT, 1,198 GitHub stars) is a local-first, open-source alternative to Grok Bot, OpenAI dots and Claude Duet: it runs on your own Windows, macOS or Linux machine, reaches GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and 70+ more models through one Modelflare account billed per token, and works in the background with approval cards for anything outside its workspace. This guide installs v0.1.16, signs in to Modelflare, builds a bot with its own workspace and permissions, gives it a background task and a scheduled rule, and reaches it from a chat app, plus the Docker route for a server.
